tagline: Yellowstone to Missouri on the old Regina-Yellowstone Trail.
intro: Out of Terry on the Yellowstone, Highway 253 heads north to meet Highway 200 for Circle, and Highway 13 carries on to Wolf Point on the Missouri, 105 miles from one of the state's two big rivers to the other. It is paved all the way now. The road follows part of the old Regina-Yellowstone Trail, which Canadian tourists once took south to Yellowstone National Park.
Between the towns it is dry-land farms and prairie grass, scoria buttes and badlands. Kiosks in Terry, Circle and Wolf Point tell the local history.

moments.title: Terry
moments.text: The town began as Joubert's Landing, a supply point for freighters on the Yellowstone, and took General Alfred Terry's name when the Northern Pacific arrived in 1881.

moments.title: Circle
moments.text: The town is named for the brand a rancher here put on his cattle.

moments.title: Lewis and Clark Bridge
moments.text: When this five-span through truss opened in 1930 as the only bridge on 350 miles of the Missouri, more than 10,000 people came with five bands and fireworks.
